reasonToGo: Broken rock down the whole western side of this region and sand over the rest of it. The longest rock spine drawn anywhere runs the west; the east carries a salt floor, a stone pavement and a single ridge of sand nearly twenty kilometres long, lying over one another. No road comes onto it and nobody lives on it, so everything is carried in and everything is carried out, and a party works one side or the other and leaves the rest alone for the season.

hazards.name: The long ridge
hazards.description: The sand ridge lies with the wind rather than across it, which means it runs nearly twenty kilometres end to end and cannot be walked round inside a day. The lee face stands at the steepest angle sand will hold, and a party that digs at the foot of it brings the face down.

hazards.name: The white floor
hazards.description: The salt crust and the stone pavement lie across the east of this region together: flat, pale, and with nothing on either of them to break the light. The glare off them at midday burns a face from underneath, and there is no shade between the rock and the sand to sit it out in.

resources.name: Belt ore
resources.description: Worked out of the belt of low broken hills at the spine's foot, where the rock has already come apart and nothing has to be cut out of a face. It is the reason a party crosses this ground at all, and it is carried out on backs.

resources.name: Reg stone
resources.description: Close-packed stones polished flat with all the fine stuff blown out from between them, lifted off the pavement by the sackful and sorted at the camp. The pavement gives it up faster than a party can carry it away.

resources.name: Draa salvage
resources.description: Taken off the ridge's lee where the sand thins each season and shows what went under it. It is a poor trade by weight and a good one by luck, and nobody works it who has ore to work instead.

landmarks.name: Regwind Horn
landmarks.description: Thirty-four kilometres of unbroken rock backbone along the west of the region — the longest single spine charted anywhere in the world, of the thirteen that are charted at all. The only ways over it are the notches, and it is the wall this ground is behind.

landmarks.name: Yardang across Emberwater
landmarks.description: One of three wind-cut rock ridges standing on this ground, two and a half kilometres of it, cut to an edge on the side the wind comes from and undercut on the other. Eight are charted in the world and all eight are on Thirstwold.
